newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips decline, SAX index down 4.85 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips decline, SAX index down 4.85 pts.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed lower in flat trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, pulling the SAX index down 4.85 points to 185.78.
Brokers said the weak trading in the leading shares would continue amid a general decline in the broader market.
The heaviest Slovak issue, oil refinery Slovnaft, closed down 50 crowns at 750 crowns, but on only three shares traded.
"Slovnaft, as the leading share, shows the trend very clearly," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings. "Nobody wants to buy or sell at the moment."
Steel maker VSZ traded the biggest volume of the session on the listed market, of 2,758 shares, closing down 20 crowns at 540, but Sykora said the issue's price still artificial.
"There is a package of some 2,300 VSZ shares floating around the market at some 640 crowns, with the sole purpose of artificially boosting the price," Sykora said.
"I see the real value in VSZ at about 500," he added.
Sykora said he expected the slide could still continue as recent amendment to the securities law spreaded uncertainty among mainly foreign investors.
"For a while let us not expect sunny tommorows, but only sombre rainy todays," he added.
Overall volume increased to 220,929 shares from 181,707 shares traded on Friday, while turnover rose to 198.60 million crowns, from 79.90 million.
